transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Okonkwo, thank you for coming back in to see me. I have asked Dr. Miller to join us as a witness to this conversation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am here. I was quite surprised to be called back so soon.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I asked you to return because I made a mistake with your discharge instructions. I sent you to a follow-up clinic that does not take your insurance provider.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I see.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to be very clear that this was my error. I failed to verify the coverage before I gave you those papers, and for that, I am sincerely sorry. I take full responsibility for this mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is... disappointing. I had already arranged for my daughter to drive me. I told my community board that my health was being managed. Now I find myself in a position where I cannot even get through the door of the clinic you chose.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear how frustrating this is. It sounds like more than just a scheduling issue; it's a matter of your reputation and the commitments you've made to your family and your board.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. In my position, one cannot be seen as a man who is disorganized or whose affairs are in chaos. It is a matter of dignity.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. It is distressing to feel that your standing is compromised because of a mistake I made. Does that explain the situation clearly, or is there any part of the error you'd like me to clarify?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You have explained the error. You gave me the wrong place.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I appreciate you confirming that. Just to be absolutely certain we are on the same page, do you have any questions about why the insurance is an issue at that specific location?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No. The issue is not the insurance company. The issue is the error.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I am truly sorry for the stress this has caused you and your daughter.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now? I cannot simply wait for the problem to solve itself.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will get this sorted. We will look into it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Look into it? Does that mean I have an appointment tomorrow? Or next week?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give you a date right this second. I'll probably send an email or maybe you'll get a call.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An email. I am fifty-seven years old, doctor, not a child. I need to know where I am going and when.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. Well, we'll see what the other clinics have available. Just stay tuned for an update.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan. That is a hope.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's not ideal. We'll just try to find something that works.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My daughter is expecting a clear directive. I cannot tell her we are just waiting for an email.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will figure it out. I'll check the system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will you check the system?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sometime today. Or tomorrow. I'll just get back to you.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish their turns and does not interrupt, though pacing becomes slightly rushed toward the end.

E.justification: Error is named explicitly in the second turn, lay language is used, and comprehension is checked twice ('Does that explain the situation clearly' and 'do you have any questions').

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language ('sincerely sorry'), takes full responsibility, and maintains this accountability throughout the pushback.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('frustrating', 'distressing') and references the patient's specific concerns regarding his reputation and family.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders and vague hopes ('we'll see', 'stay tuned', 'we'll figure it out') without specific timelines or a concrete plan.
